walkthroughs.body_html:
The Global Business Environment — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Global Business Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Global Business Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
PESTLE stands for Profit, Earnings, Sales, Trade, Loans, Equity.
PESTLE analyses the internal strengths and weaknesses of a business.
The external macro-environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors affecting a business.

mcqs.q: How does HRM differ from traditional personnel management?
options: HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
HRM and personnel are exactly the same thing — just a name change.
HRM treats people as a strategic asset and integrates human resource policies with business strategy; personnel management is more administrative and reactive, handling hiring, pay and disputes.
PESTLE stands for Profit, Earnings, Sales, Trade, Loans, Equity.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.
Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.
